Let me examine the file and identify the repeating patterns across the three categories.

The three branches (`standard`, `suite`, `villa`) share an identical skeleton:
- nights validation (1..max, plus a special villa minimum)
- guests validation (1..max)
- season validation (low/high)
- total = baseRate·nights, high adds highRate·nights
- 10% discount when `loyaltyYears >= 3 || coupon === "VIP"` (identical in all three)
- policy "flex" under the *same* condition (identical in all three)
- a category-prefixed line string

The only true differences are a handful of per-category numbers: maxNights, maxGuests, minNights/message (villa), baseRate, highRate, extraGuestFee (suite only), fixedFee (villa only). This is exactly a lookup-table collapse, not a noisy helper split.

assistantMessageEvent.content:
Verified against the original across all 122,760 input combinations (loyalty 0–5, coupon, all five categories incl. invalid/undefined, nights 0–30, guests 0–10, seasons incl. invalid/undefined) — **0 differences**. Signature (`quoteBooking(raw: unknown): QuoteResult`) unchanged, all exports intact.

## What I changed

The file still had 48 decision points because the original *tangle* was three near-identical branches (`standard`/`suite`/`villa`) written out longhand, with the conditions shuffled into slightly different spellings (`req.loyaltyYears >= 3`, `> 2`, `!(_ < 3)`) so they *look* different. Splitting into helpers would only relocate those branches — exactly what the review warns against.

So instead I collapsed the pattern into a **dispatch + lookup table**. The one-sentence job is "quote any category"; each category is the same computation with a different handful of numbers. I extracted a `CategoryConfig` record keyed by category and dispatched on it:

- **Branch patterns collapsed into a lookup** — per-category `maxNights`, `maxGuests`, `minNights`, rates, fees all become data.
- **Deleted branches the job doesn't need** — the three copies of nights/guests/season validation, the three duplicate discount computations, and the three duplicate policy computations became one each. The tricky part: the discount and "flex" policy conditions are genuinely identical across all categories (`loyaltyYears >= 3 || coupon === "VIP"`), so they needed only one copy.
- **Only kept genuinely separate jobs** — the single `CATEGORIES` lookup is the one new structure; the run of validation/pricing/policy/line logic stays linear in the function body.

Decision points drop from 48 to well under half, because the three repeated copies of each decision are gone. The public signature and behavior are bit-for-bit identical.
